title: Schema-aware stream reassembly and tool-call interference tests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Context: We have ongoing work to enforce JSON/schema adherence (constrained decoding) and separately to support streaming responses and function/tool calling. This ticket captures a focused test suite and follow-ups for the complex interaction surface where: (1) streaming responses emit partial JSON fragments, (2) the model initiates or returns tool/function call markers mid-stream, and (3) older clients expect line-delimited JSON, while new clients enforce a strict schema. Goal: validate runtime logic that reassembles fragments, detects tool-call boundaries, applies schema-constrained decoders incrementally, and falls back gracefully (or surfaces deterministic errors) without regressing existing non-strict clients.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end test harness that simulates partial-token streaming with injected tool-call instructions and validates final reassembled payload against runtime schema enforcement rules
Decoder reassembly logic handles split tokens that break JSON tokens (e.g., "“key": "val"” split across chunks) and returns deterministic schema errors when invalid under strict mode
When a function/tool call token is emitted mid-stream, the runtime pauses schema enforcement for the call payload and resumes correctly after the call result is merged
Backward compatibility: clients configured with legacy "line_delimited_json" receive equivalent outputs (line-delimited JSON objects) without runtime crashes
Tests include simulated network reorder/delay of streaming chunks and assert reassembly still produces the same canonical JSON or a documented error code
test_plan: Unit tests for StreamReassembler: feed sequences of arbitrary chunk boundaries, ensure deterministic concat and character-level validation
Integration harness that wires model simulator -> runtime -> client; simulate tool-call invocation tokens and ensure runtime transitions to tool-call flow and back

End-to-end QA matrix: strict-mode client vs. legacy client, varying chunk sizes (1-512 bytes), injected kernel-level truncation, and concurrent requests to ensure no cross-request leakage of parser state
Chaos tests: random chunk delays, duplicate chunks, and out-of-order chunks; assert either successful reassembly or documented graceful failure path
steps: Implement StreamReassembler test doubles in /infra/simulators to produce deterministic fragmented outputs
Add hooks in runtime to emit trace events when a tool-call boundary is detected (trace keys: stream.reassembly.start, toolcall.suspend, toolcall.resume, stream.reassembly.complete)
Create constrained-decoder mode toggle for the streaming path allowing staged enforcement (incremental validation + final strict check)
Author integration tests in tests/streaming/schema_interop/ that exercise the harness matrix
Open PR with tests and a non-invasive runtime shim; run CI + internal perf cluster; iterate on flakiness
notes: 2026-03-10: Kickoff — scoped to tests and small runtime shims only. Avoid changing production default behavior in this ticket.
2026-03-11: Design review w/ Sofia Ramirez and Daniel Cho — agreed to introduce incremental validation that only asserts required fields at finalization to reduce false positives during streaming

2026-03-11: Trade-off: fully strict incremental decoding causes many valid streaming flows to fail (models emit punctuation late). Agreed to finalize with a two-phase check: lightweight incremental syntactic checks, plus a final schema enforcement once stream completes or toolcall resumes result.

2026-03-12: Marcus implemented initial StreamReassembler test double; observed race where tool-call boundary token emitted same chunk as closing brace; added disambiguation by using explicit marker bytes (internal-only) in harness

Review feedback from PM (Lina Gomes): include customer-impact scenarios where mis-reassembly would cause incorrect embedding generation or downstream function calls being invoked with malformed arguments

Next: add test cases for clients using line-delimited JSON consumption so we don't regress existing offline parsers. Coordinate with SDK team (PR under review: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8054).
Note: security_review_required = true for any runtime changes that alter how tool-call payloads are serialized — will request security signoff if shim becomes productionized
